subproblem.statement: Hypothesis names: (REP) and (CT) = (T1) ∧ (T2) ∧ (MM) are the first two conjuncts of the frozen type of the parent's dependency foundations (character-for-character the frozen types of the DAG theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation and cbr_measure_convergence_tools); (SL) is the frozen type of the parent's dependency slicing (cmc_slice_mass_bounds); (RU) is the frozen type of the parent's dependency restrict_unique (cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq); (MR) is the parent's first hypothesis (type of cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure); (RECT) is the frozen type of the parent's dependency rectifiable (character-for-character that of cbr_rectifiable_of_approx_tangent). Whichever are needed appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement; the parent discharges them. In words: (REP) a current T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, with M_W(T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U has a mass representation (μ, ξ): μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ(W) = M_W(T) for open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 provided also M_W(∂T) < ∞ (boundaryMassOn) for open W ⊂⊂ U; (MR) M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of T in an open U and open W; (SL) for T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) with admissible representations (μ, ξ) of T and (μ', ξ') of ∂T and an L-Lipschitz f there are currents A_t, B_t with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t = B_t on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h < f < t}) and ∫⁻_{(a,b)}M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ Lμ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W; (RU) an identity ∫ξ₁(ω)dμ₁ = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫ξ₃(ω)dμ₃ between admissible pairs, valid for all test forms on an open U, remains valid with all integrals restricted to any Borel set; (T1) measures μ_j with sup_jμ_j(K) < ∞ on compacts have a subsequence converging to a Borel μ finite on compacts (against continuous compactly supported functions; limsup on compacts ≤ μ; liminf on open sets ≥ μ); (T2) if X_j ⇀ X with admissible representations (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ_X, ξ_X), limsup_jμ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) on compacts for a Borel μ finite on compacts, f continuous and μ{f = t} = 0, then ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X for every ω; (MM) if μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞ and Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t−h < f < t}) for t ∈ (a, b), then some measurable g has liminf_jZ_j(t) ≤ g(t) for a.e. t ∈ (a, b) and ∫⁻_{(a,b)}g ≤ L·liminf_jμ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}); (RECT) a Borel M with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ having approximate tangent spaces Q(x) at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M with x ↦ p_{Q(x)} Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable is countably n-rectifiable. Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω_n = unitBallVolume n, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α for covectors; an admissible representation (μ, ξ) of a current X in ℝ^P is a Borel measure μ finite on compact sets and a μ-a.e. strongly measurable ξ with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e., X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for every test form. ISP (integer slice property) of Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P): for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of Y and (μ', ξ') of ∂Y and every Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, for L¹-a.e. t, all A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms have ∂A − B integer multiplicity. SLIM_{P,d}: if X_i, X ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), every X_i has ISP, sup_i(M_W(X_i) + M_W(∂X_i)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure, and X_i ⇀ X, then X has ISP (hypothesis of the parent). LD_{P,d}: there is η₀ > 0 such that for every C ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂C = 0 and ISP, every Borel μ finite on compacts with μ(W) = M_W(C) for open W and every μ-a.e. strongly measurable ξ with |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e. and C(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, liminf_{r↓0}μ(B_r(x))/(ω_{d+1}r^{d+1}) ≥ η₀ for μ-a.e. x (hypothesis of the parent). For a ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 let η(y) := dilation a λ y = λ⁻¹(y − a); X' ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) is a dilation of X ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) if X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω') for all test m-forms ω, ω' with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y. Assume (REP), (MR), (SL), (RU), (CT). Let P, d ∈ ℕ, n := d+1, and assume SLIM_{P,d} (if X_i ⇀ X in 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), each X_i has ISP and sup_i(M_W(X_i) + M_W(∂X_i)) < ∞ for open W with compact closure, then X has ISP; hypothesis of the parent) and LD_{P,d} (there is η₀ > 0 such that for every C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂C = 0 and ISP, every Borel μ finite on compacts with μ(W) = M_W(C) for open W and every μ-a.e. strongly measurable ξ with |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e. and C(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, liminf_{r↓0}μ(B_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≥ η₀ for μ-a.e. x; hypothesis of the parent). Let Γ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂Γ = 0 and ISP; μ a finite Borel measure with μ(W) = M_W(Γ) for open W; M Borel with Hⁿ(M) < ∞; θ Borel and ζ strongly measurable with μ = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density ofReal∘θ, θ > 0 on M, |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and for each x ∈ M some β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζ(x)(β) = 1; Γ(ω) = ∫_Mθζ(ω)dHⁿ for all ω. Let a ∈ M and η₁ > 0 with liminf_{r↓0}μ(B_r(a))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≥ η₁, limsup_{r↓0}Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≤ 1 and (∫⁻_{M∩B̄_r(a)}‖θζ − θ(a)ζ(a)‖dHⁿ)/(ω_nrⁿ) → 0 as r ↓ 0. Then there is a subspace Q such that M has approximate tangent space Q at a (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M a Q, in particular dim Q = n), ζ(a) is a unit orientation of Q, and θ(a) is a natural number.

The hypotheses (REP), (MR), (SL), (RU), (CT) and SLIM_{P,d} of this statement are passed to the siblings that require them ((BL) needs (SL), (RU), (CT), SLIM_{P,d}; (WG) needs (REP), (SL), (CT); (PI) needs (MR), (SL)); LD_{P,d} is used in step 3(b).
1. Notation. n := d + 1, θ₀ := θ(a) > 0 (a ∈ M), ζ₀ := ζ(a), ω_n := unitBallVolume n; η₀' > 0 is the constant provided by LD_{P,d}.
2. Plane uniqueness (parent Step 6, final remark). If v, v' are orthonormal n-families in ℝ^P with β(v) = β(v') for every n-covector β, then span v = span v'. For n = 0 both spans are {0}. Let n ≥ 1. For w ∈ ℝ^P and an (n−1)-covector α (a scalar if n = 1) let w^♭∧α be the n-covector (u_1, …, u_n) ↦ Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}⟨w, u_j⟩α(u_1, …, û_j, …, u_n) (multilinear and alternating; in Lean ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ w).smulRight α), whose value is Σ_j(−1)^j⟨w, u_j⟩α(Fin.removeNth j u) with 0-based j). Then (w^♭∧α)(v) = ⟨Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}α(v^{(j)})v_j, w⟩ with v^{(j)} := (v_1, …, v̂_j, …, v_n), and likewise for v'. As the two evaluations agree for every w, Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}α(v^{(j)})v_j = Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}α(v'^{(j)})v'_j for every α. Take α := β_{v^{(i)}}, β_{v^{(i)}}(u) := det(⟨u_s, v^{(i)}_r⟩)_{s,r} (an (n−1)-covector, e.g. from cbr_ci_cp_pr_inner_det_covector; for n = 1 it is the constant 0-covector 1): β_{v^{(i)}}(v^{(j)}) = δ_{ij} (for j ≠ i the family v^{(j)} contains v_i, orthogonal to every member of v^{(i)}, so the Gram matrix has a zero row; for j = i it is the identity). Hence (−1)^{i−1}v_i ∈ span v' for every i, so span v ⊆ span v', and by symmetry span v = span v'.
3. Claim. For every sequence (λ_i) with λ_i > 0 and λ_i → 0 there are a strictly increasing φ and an orthonormal v = (v_1, …, v_n) such that ζ₀(β) = β(v) for all n-covectors β, ∫_{blowUpMap a λ_{φ(k)} '' M}f dHⁿ → ∫_{span v}f dHⁿ for every continuous compactly supported f, and θ₀ is a natural number.

Apply LD_{P,d} to C with the measure θ₀ν := ofReal(θ₀)·ν and the constant field ζ₀: ∂C = 0; θ₀ν is finite on compacts; M_W(C) = θ₀ν(W) for open W; the constant field is strongly measurable with |ζ₀(α)| ≤ |α|; C(ω) = θ₀∫ζ₀(ω)dν = ∫ζ₀(ω)d(θ₀ν) (integral_smul_measure, (ofReal θ₀).toReal = θ₀); C has ISP. Writing (ofReal(θ₀)·ν)(B)/D = ofReal(θ₀)·(ν(B)/D) (Measure.smul_apply, mul_div_assoc), and using that multiplication by the finite positive constant ofReal(θ₀) commutes with liminf in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.liminf_const_mul_of_ne_zero_of_ne_top), we get ofReal(η₀') ≤ ofReal(θ₀)·liminf_{r↓0}ν(B_r(y))/(ω_nrⁿ), hence liminf_{r↓0}ν(B_r(y))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≥ ofReal(η₀'/θ₀) for ν-a.e. y (ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos, ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul').

4. The plane. Apply the claim to λ_i := 1/(i + 1); let v be the resulting orthonormal family and Q := span v. finrank Q = n (finrank_span_eq_card; orthonormal families are linearly independent). ζ₀ is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf with the frame v and the + sign: ζ₀(α) = α(v) for all α), and θ(a) = θ₀ is a natural number.
5. Approximate tangent space (parent Step 9). Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), F(r) := ∫_{blowUpMap a r '' M}f dHⁿ and L₀ := ∫_Qf dHⁿ. Since 𝓝[>]0 is countably generated, by Filter.tendsto_of_subseq_tendsto it suffices that every sequence r_j tending to 0 within (0, ∞) has a subsequence along which F → L₀. Given such (r_j), choose j₀ with r_j > 0 for all j ≥ j₀ and apply the claim to λ_i := r_{i+j₀} (positive, tending to 0): a strictly increasing φ and an orthonormal v' with ζ₀(β) = β(v') for all β and F(λ_{φ(k)}) → ∫_{span v'}f dHⁿ. Hence F(r) → L₀ as r → 0⁺ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), which together with finrank Q = n is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M a Q. With step 4, Q has all the asserted properties. ∎

For any blow-up sequence, (BL) gives a limit C = θ(a)ζ(a)ν with ISP; LD_{P,d} applied to (θ(a)ν, ζ(a)) gives the lower density of ν.
(CP) makes ν a finite sum of parallel planes with ζ(a) = evaluation on v; (WG) gives every weight ≥ 1, so ν = Hⁿ⌞span v; (PI) gives θ(a) ∈ ℕ.
Plane uniqueness and the subsequence criterion give HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M a (span v) and the unit orientation.
